properties.state: {"description":"The capture half of KPPs, and the half a person actually touches. Anthony, 2026-07-25: the user says \\\"the system should be able to perform X\\\"; the agent, acting as the systems-engineering SME the user is not required to be (req:no-se-knowledge), recognises the shape of inviolable intent and asks — that sounds like something that MUST be met, is it? — and the user confirms or declines. WHY THE AGENT MUST NOT DECIDE IT: criticality is a claim about consequence, not about wording. Whether missing a threshold FAILS THE EFFORT depends on mission, contract and money that the graph does not hold and the agent cannot see. An agent that promoted a requirement to KPP on its own would be asserting the user's stake in their own project, which is the same forgery dec:certainty-derived forbids for requirement status — and worse here, because a KPP outranks every ordinary gap and would drag the whole detector's ranking with it. So: the agent PROPOSES, the human DISPOSES, and nothing enters as a KPP without the user's word. WHAT THE AGENT CAN LEGITIMATELY NOTICE, and it is more than intuition. A statement carrying a unit-bearing threshold (500 miles, 3000 pounds, 500 milliseconds) is already shaped like a KPP and may simply be unmodelled — the quantity/limit/direction triple has somewhere to go. Language of necessity ('must', 'shall', 'no less than') against language of preference ('should', 'aims to') is a real signal in acquisition prose. And a requirement whose failure the user has elsewhere described as fatal is a candidate the graph itself can surface. THE QUESTION MUST CARRY THE CONSEQUENCE, not just the label: asking 'is this a KPP?' invites a shrug, whereas asking 'if the system missed this by ten percent, would the effort have failed?' is answerable by someone who has never heard the term — which is the test req:no-se-knowledge sets. On confirmation the agent sets category kpp, and should ask for the threshold and, where one exists, the objective; on decline it stays an ordinary Requirement and the offer is not repeated. PLANNED.","is_entry_point":false,"is_exit_point":false,"name":"Notice when a stated need is really a KPP, and ask","provenance":"authored","status":"planned","tier":"operational"}
